We are pleased to announce that all outputs related to our first milestone have been successfully completed. Detailed information can be found in the GitHub documentation at marlowe-web-integration/README.md at main · Erickrs2/marlowe-web-integration (github.com). 
The documentation includes an introduction to Marlowe, an overview of our roadmap, a list of discussions and bugs encountered during testing the TypeScript SDK, and an explanation of the framework we used for designing, creating, testing, and integrating our smart contracts.
We are excited to share that we have already made this output available to the entire Cardano and Marlowe community. This marks the first time a complete end-to-end example of a Marlowe smart contract, utilizing the latest features—Runtime 1.0, TS-SDK 0.4, and Next.js 14 app router framework—has been demonstrated. We are proud of this initial achievement.
The deployed Dapp can be found here: https://marlowe-web-integration.vercel.app/

ms.report:
We are pleased to announce that all outputs related to our third milestone have been successfully completed. Detailed information can be found in the GitHub documentation at 
marlowe-web-integration/README.md at main · ErickRomeroDev/marlowe-web-integration (github.com) 
During milestone three, we tested and fully integrated new features such as Merklelization, annotation, and the use of custom oracles. With Merklelization, we were able to include contract steps accommodating up to 7 payments. Annotations allowed us to efficiently filter between roles-address and open-role actions. Additionally, we implemented custom oracles, allowing the selection of an auditor by choice.
The documentation includes the continuation of our roadmap, an extended list of discussions and bugs encountered during testing the TypeScript SDK, and an explanation of the framework we used for designing, creating, testing, and integrating our smart contracts using Nodejs and Next.js
You can find the deployed Dapp here: https://marlowe.eddalabs.io/
